nodes.label: Robustness Over Accuracy
nodes.rationale: The governing conviction of the site, repeated in three places: accuracy is necessary but robustness is required; a notebook accuracy of 92% is the beginning, never the verdict; the model is finished only when it works in the world. Benchmarks are not chased for their own sake - systems that survive contact with the real world are.

nodes.label: AI Tells (Forbidden Patterns)
nodes.rationale: Signatures the model defaults to when trying to look designed: neon glows, pure black, Inter as default, three equal feature cards, Jane Doe names, Acme-style brands, fake-perfect numbers, version labels in the hero, section-number eyebrows, decorative status dots, scroll cues, locale strips, photo-credit captions as decoration, fake version footers, scoring bars.

nodes.label: Apple Liquid Glass Web Approximation
nodes.rationale: Apple documents Liquid Glass for Apple platforms only and there is no official liquid-glass.css for the web. A web approximation uses backdrop-filter, layered borders and highlight overlays, must be labeled an approximation, and falls back to solid fill under prefers-reduced-transparency (uneven support).

nodes.label: Block Library Contract
nodes.rationale: Reference vocabulary names patterns; the block library implements them with real props, motion specs and code sketches, one block per file, each standalone and each passing the Pre-Flight Check. Frontmatter declares dial compatibility, when_to_use, not_for and stack.

nodes.label: Color Calibration (One Accent, Lila Rule)
nodes.rationale: Max one accent, saturation under 80%, neutral bases (Zinc/Slate/Stone). AI purple-blue glow discouraged unless the brand asks, then executed with intent rather than generic gradient slop. One palette per project, no warm/cool gray fluctuation.

nodes.label: Content Density Rules
nodes.rationale: Cut ruthlessly: short headline (8 words max) plus short sub-paragraph (25 words) plus one visual or CTA. No data-dump sections; long lists need a different UI component rather than a longer list, and fake-precise engineering numbers without real data are banned.

nodes.label: Dark Mode Protocol and Token Strategy
nodes.rationale: Dual-mode by default with an explicit carve-out: never assume light-only unless the brief is print-emulating editorial. Pick either the Tailwind dark variant or CSS variables, enforce contrast, hierarchy parity and brand fidelity, no pure #000000 or #ffffff.
nodes.norm_label: dark mode protocol and token strategy

nodes.label: Default Architecture (RSC, Tailwind v4, Motion)
nodes.rationale: Unless the design read picks a real design system: React/Next.js with Server Components, Tailwind v4, Motion imported from motion/react, and next/font or self-hosted @font-face. Never link Google Fonts via link in production. Motion, scroll listeners and pointer physics must be isolated in use client leaf components.

nodes.label: Brief to Design System Map
nodes.rationale: Do not invent CSS for things that have an official package and do not pretend an aesthetic trend is an official system. When the brief is an aesthetic (bento, brutalism, editorial, kinetic type) build with native CSS and label borrowed inspiration honestly.

nodes.label: GSAP Horizontal-Pan Skeleton
nodes.rationale: Canonical HorizontalPan client component: wrapper pinned, inner track translated by scrollWidth minus innerWidth, start top top, end +distance, scrub 1, invalidateOnRefresh, min-h-[100dvh] track.

nodes.label: Icon Library Policy
nodes.rationale: Priority order Phosphor, HugeIcons, Radix, Tabler; lucide-react discouraged unless explicitly requested. Never hand-roll SVG icon paths, one family per project, standardize strokeWidth globally.

nodes.label: Image and Visual Asset Priority Order
nodes.rationale: Landing pages and portfolios are visual products. Priority: image-generation tool first, real web images (picsum.photos with descriptive seeds) second, tell the user last. Div-based fake screenshots and hand-rolled decorative SVGs are banned; even minimalist sites need 2-3 real images.
nodes.norm_label: image and visual asset priority order

nodes.label: Layout Discipline Hard Rules
nodes.rationale: Hero must fit the initial viewport (headline 2 lines, subtext 20 words, CTAs visible), hero top padding capped at pt-24, max four text elements in the hero, navigation on one line at 80px max, bento grids need rhythm and exact cell count, no layout family twice, max two image+text splits in a row, explicit mobile collapse per section.

nodes.label: Performance and Core Web Vitals Guardrails
nodes.rationale: Animate only transform and opacity, LCP under 2.5s, INP under 200ms, CLS under 0.1, grain filters only on fixed pointer-events-none layers, z-index used strictly for systemic layers and documented as a scale.
nodes.norm_label: performance and core web vitals guardrails

nodes.label: Final Pre-Flight Check Matrix
nodes.rationale: Mechanical last filter before shipping; if a single checkbox cannot be honestly ticked, the page is not done.

nodes.label: Redesign Protocol and Audit
nodes.rationale: Detect greenfield vs preserve vs overhaul first, audit brand tokens, IA, content blocks, patterns to keep and retire, the dial reading of the existing site and the SEO baseline (SEO migration is the number one redesign risk). Never change URL slugs, nav labels, form field names, wordmark or legal copy silently.

nodes.label: Reference Vocabulary (Pattern Names)
nodes.rationale: A vocabulary, not a library: hero paradigms, navigation, layout and grids, cards, scroll animations, galleries, typography and micro-interactions, so the agent can name and reach for a pattern instead of inventing one. Implementations live in the Block Library.

nodes.label: Motion Scroll-Reveal Stagger Skeleton
nodes.rationale: RevealStagger with motion.li whileInView, initial opacity 0 and y 24, viewport once amount 0.3, duration 0.6, delay i times 0.06, ease [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1]. Preferred over GSAP for simple enter-on-scroll; save GSAP for pin and scrub work.

nodes.label: GSAP Sticky-Stack Skeleton
nodes.rationale: Canonical StickyStack client component: start top top, pin true, every card except the last pinned, scale and opacity driven by the next card's trigger, gsap.context with ctx.revert cleanup, reduced-motion early return.

nodes.label: Three Dials (Design Variance, Motion Intensity, Visual Density)
nodes.rationale: Every layout, motion and density decision is gated by three global variables with baseline 8 / 6 / 4, inferred from the design read. Cross-references use these exact names; never invent aliases.
nodes.norm_label: three dials (design variance, motion intensity, visual density)

nodes.label: Accessibility and Craft Baseline
nodes.rationale: Warm paper plus ink delivers AA contrast at body sizes. Semantic landmarks, skip link, real alt text, aria-labelled links, keyboard-visible focus in accent, scroll-margin for anchored sections.

nodes.label: Collage and Imperfection
nodes.rationale: Tactile plates (halftone rasters, scanlines, iso-contour fields, wireframe networks, spectrum bars) generated procedurally as stand-ins for photography or layered behind printed imagery; slight rotation -1.5deg, uneven rules, oversized bleeding numerals. Imperfection applied deliberately, once per view.

nodes.label: Implementation Pipeline
nodes.rationale: A typed brief (inputs.json) is composed by pure renderers into one static HTML file: compose in, print out.

nodes.label: Layout Grammar (12-Column Asymmetric Editorial Grid)
nodes.rationale: 12-column grid with generous margins, composed asymmetry with 12-16% offsets, numbered kickers with hairlines, Fig. 01 captions inside the composition, mono metadata tables ruled by hairlines. Never chips, pills or progress bars. Whitespace is a material.

nodes.label: Material and Colour Token System
nodes.rationale: Monochrome foundations with one warm accent; ink is warm-black, never pure. Tokens: paper #F4F0E6, paper-deep #E9E2D1, ink #17150F, ink-2 #3E382B, ink-3 #6E6554, rule #CEC4AE, accent #E24A1F, accent-2 #2E4A9E.

nodes.label: Editorial Motion System (Scroll Reveal + Headroom Nav)
nodes.rationale: Elements lift 26px and fade over 0.8s with a staggered 0.06s per sibling, never more than one in-production reveal per viewport. Masthead hides on scroll-down, returns on scroll-up or at the top. No autoplay, no marquees, no parallax scrims, no blur glass.
nodes.norm_label: editorial motion system (scroll reveal + headroom nav)

nodes.label: Procedural Collage Plate Fallback
nodes.rationale: The composer prefers raster assets when present and falls back to procedural plates, so imagery never becomes a hard dependency.

nodes.label: Self-Contained Single HTML Output
nodes.rationale: One self-contained HTML file mirrored to dist/index.html and apps/landing-page/index.html so any static host can serve it.

nodes.label: Three-Voice Typography (Fraunces / Archivo / Space Mono)
nodes.rationale: Three voices, never more. Fraunces variable serif for display (wght 560-620, -0.02em), Archivo grotesk for body and labels, Space Mono for captions and metadata. Fluid scale from hero clamp(3.4rem, 9vw, 8.2rem) down to 0.72rem caption at 0.14em tracking.

nodes.label: Optional gpt-image-2 Collage Asset Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Requires an OpenAI API key with gpt-image-2 access, writes 16 PNGs to scripts/assets/collage/, supports --dry to preview prompts, then re-composes to fold the rasters in.

nodes.label: Static Host Deployment and CNAME
nodes.rationale: dist/index.html (or the mirror) is a static file deployable to GitHub Pages, Netlify, Vercel or Cloudflare Pages; current deployment is santhosh_sunkara_portfolio.com via a repo-root CNAME.

nodes.label: MIT License (System Free, Content Personal)
nodes.rationale: The Atelier Zero system is free to adapt under MIT; the portfolio content in inputs.json stays personal to Santhosh Sunkara.

nodes.label: Nine Movements Page Structure
nodes.rationale: Nine numbered sections with stable anchors (#top, #manifesto, #work, #about, #experience, #studio, #credentials, #journal, #contact). Numbered movements make the scroll read as an edited publication.

nodes.label: Client-Side Output Features
nodes.rationale: Headroom nav hiding on scroll-down, staggered scroll-reveal via IntersectionObserver, active-section highlighting in the masthead, details/summary mobile menu fallback, plus accessibility affordances.

nodes.label: Atelier Zero Visual Language Summary
nodes.rationale: Paper ground #F4F0E6, warm black ink #17150F, single vermilion accent #E24A1F at about 5%, Fraunces + Archivo + Space Mono, 12-column asymmetric grid, procedural SVG plates plus optional gpt-image-2 rasters.

nodes.label: design-taste-frontend (Anti-Slop Frontend Skill)
nodes.rationale: Anti-slop frontend skill for landing pages, portfolios and redesigns: read the brief, infer the design direction, ship interfaces that do not look templated. Not for dashboards, data tables or multi-step product UI. Every rule is contextual, none fires automatically.

nodes.label: Atelier Zero Editorial Portfolio System
nodes.rationale: The site is treated as an independent design publication (Monocle / Apartamento / Etudes Studio) rather than a conventional personal website.

nodes.label: inputs.json (Typed Portfolio Brief)
nodes.rationale: The typed brief holding person, manifesto, projects and other content; content is separated from rendering.

nodes.label: scripts/compose.js (Composer CLI)
nodes.rationale: Pure compose(inputs) -> html with the CLI at the bottom; resolves assets then emits HTML.

nodes.label: scripts/generate-assets.js (Optional gpt-image-2 Generation)
nodes.rationale: Optional, produces up to 16 bespoke collage assets in the Atelier Zero style; the composer works without them.

nodes.label: scripts/lib/plates.js (Procedural Collage Plates)
nodes.rationale: Renders the halftone, scanline, iso-contour and wireframe plates described in the collage section.

nodes.label: scripts/lib/sections.js (Pure Section Renderers)
nodes.rationale: Section renderers kept pure so each movement renders in isolation.

nodes.label: scripts/lib/tokens.js (Design Tokens and Helpers)
nodes.rationale: Holds the design tokens and helpers declared in the colour and typography sections of the spec.

nodes.label: Atelier Zero Portfolio (Santhosh Sunkara)
nodes.rationale: An editorial, magazine-style personal portfolio built with the Atelier Zero visual language, a single self-contained HTML file composed from a typed brief.

nodes.label: Anti-Default Discipline
nodes.rationale: Do not default to AI-purple gradients, centered hero over dark mesh, three equal feature cards, glassmorphism everywhere, infinite-loop micro-animations, Inter plus slate-900. These are the LLM defaults; reach past them deliberately from the design read.

nodes.label: Brief Inference and Design Read
nodes.rationale: Most LLM design output is bad because the model jumps to a default aesthetic instead of reading the room. Signals: page kind, vibe words, reference signals, audience, existing brand assets, quiet constraints (which override aesthetic preference). Output a one-line design read before any code and ask at most one clarifying question.

nodes.label: Color Consistency Lock
nodes.rationale: Once an accent is chosen for a page it is used on the whole page: a warm-grey site does not suddenly get a blue CTA in section 7, a rose-accented site does not get a teal footer badge. Pick one accent, lock it, audit every component.

nodes.label: Copy Self-Audit
nodes.rationale: Re-read every visible string before shipping and flag broken grammar, unclear referents, AI-hallucinated wordplay and mock-poetic micro-meta. AI-generated cute copy is worse than boring copy; when unsure, replace with a plain functional sentence.

nodes.label: Em-Dash Ban
nodes.rationale: The em-dash is the model's signature stylistic crutch and the number one visual Tell in production tests. Zero em-dashes anywhere visible, en-dashes banned as separators too, only the regular hyphen permitted. Phrasing is binary, not use sparingly.

nodes.label: Eyebrow Restraint Rule
nodes.rationale: Every AI-built site puts an uppercase tracking micro-label above every section header, producing templated rhythm. Hard rule: maximum one eyebrow per three sections, hero counts as one, checked mechanically against ceil(sectionCount / 3).

nodes.label: Forbidden Animation Patterns (Scroll Listener Ban)
nodes.rationale: window.addEventListener scroll and window.scrollY in React state are hard bans: they run every frame, are jank-prone and re-render the tree. Use Motion useScroll, GSAP ScrollTrigger, IntersectionObserver or CSS scroll-driven animations.

nodes.label: Motion Must Be Motivated
nodes.rationale: Every animation must answer what it communicates: hierarchy, storytelling, feedback or state transition. It looked cool is invalid. Motion claimed must equal motion shown: if MOTION_INTENSITY > 4 the page must actually move, else drop the dial to 3. Marquees are allowed at most once per page.

nodes.label: Official-Package Honesty Rule
nodes.rationale: If the brief reads as a known design system, install the official package. Do not hand-recreate its CSS, do not import its tokens then override 90% of them, and never mix two systems in one tree.

nodes.label: Page Theme Lock (One Theme Per Page)
nodes.rationale: The page has one theme and sections do not invert; the user must not feel they walked into a different website mid-scroll. One deliberate full theme switch is allowed per page, and the theme is set once in layout.tsx or the page root.
nodes.norm_label: page theme lock (one theme per page)

nodes.label: Premium-Consumer Warm-Paper Palette Ban
nodes.rationale: Warm beige/cream plus brass/clay/oxblood/ochre plus espresso ink is the banned default for premium-consumer briefs because every generated site with it looks the same. Rotate families (cold luxury, forest, black and tan, cobalt, terracotta, olive) and never ship the same warm-craft palette twice in a row.

nodes.label: Mandatory Reduced-Motion Handling
nodes.rationale: Any motion above MOTION_INTENSITY 3 must honor prefers-reduced-motion; infinite loops, parallax, scroll hijack and magnetic physics collapse to static. In Motion wrap with useReducedMotion, in CSS gate behind prefers-reduced-motion media queries.

nodes.label: Serif Discipline (Fraunces Banned as Default)
nodes.rationale: The default mental model that creative brief equals serif is the single most-tested AI tell. Serif is acceptable only when the brand names a serif or the family is genuinely editorial/publication and the specific serif can be justified. Fraunces and Instrument_Serif are specifically banned as defaults.

nodes.label: Shape Consistency Lock (One Radius Scale)
nodes.rationale: Pick one corner-radius scale for the page and follow it everywhere; mixed systems only with a documented rule. Round buttons in a square layout or square cards on a pill-button page is broken design.

nodes.label: State Rules (No useState for Continuous Values)
nodes.rationale: useState re-renders the whole React tree on every change and collapses on mobile, so continuous input (mouse position, scroll progress, pointer physics) must use Motion's useMotionValue / useTransform / useScroll. Global state only to avoid deep prop drilling.
nodes.norm_label: state rules (no usestate for continuous values)

nodes.label: Accent Rationing (5% Rule)
nodes.rationale: Accent is reserved for numbers, one underline, the availability dot and the contact arrow; never more than about 5% of any viewport painted accent, so vermilion stays the one loud note.

nodes.label: Curator-Reader Point of View
nodes.rationale: The reader is a curator, not a user. The page should feel like a printed monograph that happens to scroll: numbered movements, oversized headlines, marginalia, figures with captions, thin rules, deliberate asymmetry, one restrained accent. Tempo matters more than density.

nodes.label: Pure-Function Compose Core
nodes.rationale: compose(inputs) -> html is pure with the CLI at the bottom of the file, keeping rendering deterministic and the output reproducible.

nodes.label: Static Reduced-Motion Fallback
nodes.rationale: prefers-reduced-motion renders everything static and visible, so motion is never load-bearing for comprehension.

nodes.label: No-Frameworks Vanilla ES Module Build
nodes.rationale: Vanilla ES modules with inline CSS/JS so the artifact runs in any modern browser and stays a single deployable file; npm is only needed for lint.

nodes.label: Pure-Function Core compose(inputs, ctx) to html
nodes.rationale: No I/O, deterministic. Context is passed in rather than read from the filesystem, which is what makes the whole page reproducible from a typed brief.
nodes.norm_label: pure-function core compose(inputs, ctx) to html

nodes.label: AI/ML Engineer (Target Role)
nodes.rationale: Career goal is developing reliable and scalable machine learning solutions, which is why the resume stacks breadth across classical ML, deep learning, CV and GenAI.

nodes.label: API Integration
nodes.rationale: ML systems are exposed as services via APIs so trained models can be consumed by other applications rather than run as isolated scripts.

nodes.label: Coordinate-Based Frame Optimization
nodes.rationale: Tracks landmark coordinates across frames so only gesture-relevant regions are reprocessed, which is what allows 15 FPS real-time gesture handling.

nodes.label: Embedding Model
nodes.rationale: Converts queries and documents into vectors so contextual, meaning-based retrieval is possible for response generation.

nodes.label: Personalized Precaution Recommendations
nodes.rationale: Bridges the gap between model output and human use — the ML prediction is only valuable to a patient as actionable guidance, so classification output is mapped into precautions.

nodes.label: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
nodes.rationale: Retrieval is bolted onto generation so an LLM answers from indexed support documents — contextual, grounded answers instead of hallucinated or generic replies.

nodes.label: RAG-Based Customer Support Chatbot (Dec 2025)
nodes.rationale: A vector database plus an embedding model were added so responses are grounded in retrieved e-commerce context rather than model memory; reached 90% query-resolution accuracy for automated customer support.

nodes.label: Real-Time Object Detection Engine (Mar 2025)
nodes.rationale: Single-stage detectors (YOLO and SSD) were selected over multi-stage ones so live OpenCV video could be processed in real time; 80% detection accuracy under varied lighting and motion.

nodes.label: Sign-Speak: The Silent Communicator (Jun 2024)
nodes.rationale: An end-to-end vision pipeline removes the need for speech input; coordinate-based frame optimization was the design choice that held gesture processing at 15 FPS.

nodes.label: Spam Email Detection System (Oct 2023)
nodes.rationale: Naive Bayes and Logistic Regression were paired as lightweight probabilistic/linear text classifiers — cheap to train and interpret — reaching 98% accuracy on the spam classification pipeline.

nodes.label: Spatial Feature Extraction
nodes.rationale: Optimized specifically to cut inference latency and improve real-time computer vision performance during the Edunet internship.

nodes.label: Stroke Risk Prediction from MRI Scans (Sep 2025)
nodes.rationale: A CNN was chosen for spatial MRI pattern recognition (90% accuracy), and predictions were deliberately converted into personalized precaution recommendations so raw model output becomes actionable clinical guidance.
nodes.norm_label: stroke risk prediction from mri scans (sep 2025)

nodes.label: Vector Database
nodes.rationale: Chosen as the retrieval substrate for the chatbot so semantically similar support content can be fetched quickly and at scale.

nodes.label: Workflow Automation
nodes.rationale: Chosen to remove repetitive manual steps in ML delivery by wiring steps into repeatable automated pipelines.

nodes.label: Filled Brand Mark Style
nodes.rationale: Third-party social logos (Bluesky, Discord, GitHub, X) are baked as solid filled paths in near-black #08060d, not recolored to the accent palette, because trademarked brand marks must keep their recognizable silhouette and official presentation. Visual cohesion with the rest of the site comes from matched optical size inside the sprite rather than from recoloring.

nodes.label: Stroked Accent Line Icon Style
nodes.rationale: First-party UI affordances (documentation, social) use fill=none with a 1.35px stroke in accent purple #aa3bff, round linecaps and round linejoins. The shared weight, cap style and accent token make them read as one family and let them inherit the theme accent, which filled brand marks deliberately cannot do.

nodes.label: SVG Symbol Sprite (icons.svg)
nodes.rationale: All six icons are declared once as <symbol> elements with their own viewBox in a single static sprite, so path data is never duplicated and each icon is instantiated by reference. Brand marks keep their baked fill (#08060d) and are drawn at 1:1, while the line-art icons use stroke=currentColor-equivalent accent (#aa3bff) at 1.35px with round caps/joins, so the same sprite serves both third-party logos and first-party UI affordances.

nodes.label: Hero Portrait Framing Pattern (Rotated Card + Floating Glass Chips)
nodes.rationale: The photo is square so it can sit inside a tall rounded card (h-80 w-72 through md:h-[30rem] md:w-[25rem]) with object-cover and no visible letterboxing. The deployment wraps it in a rotated gradient border plus a glass surface, and floats two animated glass chips over it ('Focus: Deep Learning', 'Specialty: Computer Vision'). The mural's diagonal yellow band visually rhymes with the rotate-3 offset frame, so the busy background reads as intentional depth rather than noise behind a face.
nodes.norm_label: hero portrait framing pattern (rotated card + floating glass chips)

nodes.label: Professional Headshot Convention (Framing, Attire, Gaze)
nodes.rationale: The photo deliberately follows the standard professional headshot recipe - head-and-shoulders crop, light grey button-down instead of a logo tee, direct eye contact with a slight closed-mouth smile, and a square 1:1 aspect ratio. This buys instant credibility and approachability while staying readable when the image is scaled down into a small framed card, which is exactly how a portfolio hero uses it. Choosing a high-chroma yellow/white/black mural wall rather than a blurred neutral studio backdrop keeps the portrait from looking like a generic stock photo and ties the subject to the site's electric-violet/tertiary accent language.
